items.title: Career Toolkit (Talent Suite)
items.channel: LinkedIn - company page, Ella's profile and Open to Work outreach
items.notes:
Free Career Toolkit for job seekers: CV Health Check, Job Match Score, Tailored CV Rewrite, Interview Prep Pack and the free screening-safe CV checklist.

Goal: grow the talent pool with people who are actively looking, and let the paid recruiter services sell themselves once people see the value. No prices in any LinkedIn content.

Tracking: every link in this campaign carries a source tag (li-company, li-ella, li-outreach) so sign-ups show by channel on this row and in CRM > Talent Suite users.

Boost plan: run the posts organically for 2 weeks. Pick the 1 or 2 posts with the best engagement rate (reactions + comments + clicks divided by impressions), then boost the winner with a small daily budget for 7 days, objective Website visits, audience UK job seekers in our sectors. Compare cost per sign-up against organic before spending more.

items.title: How screening software reads your CV
items.next_step: Run a free CV Health Check
items.body:
Your CV has about 6 seconds with a person. But first it has to get past a machine.

Here's what screening software struggles with:

▪ Tables, columns and text boxes that scramble when the file is read
▪ Job titles that don't match the words in the advert
▪ Skills buried in paragraphs instead of shown with evidence
▪ Headers and footers holding your contact details
▪ Creative layouts that look great to you and blank to the system

None of that says anything about how good you are at the job. It just stops you getting the chance to prove it.

Our free CV Health Check scores your CV the way screening software and hiring managers see it, then tells you exactly what to fix first.

Two minutes. No cost. Honest answers.

items.title: Stop applying blind - Job Match Score
items.next_step: Score your match before you apply
items.body:
Applying for 50 jobs and hearing nothing back?

It's rarely a numbers problem. It's usually a match problem.

Before you hit apply on the next one, check three things:

1. Does your CV show evidence of the top 3 requirements in the advert?
2. Does your most recent job title make sense next to the role you're applying for?
3. Would a hiring manager know in one glance why you fit?

Our free Job Match Score does this for you. Paste the advert, add your CV, and it shows which requirements you evidence, which you're missing, and whether it's worth applying at all.

Fewer applications. Better ones. More replies.

items.title: Free screening-safe CV checklist
items.body:
A quick checklist before you send your CV anywhere:

☐ Saved as a Word file or simple PDF
☐ No tables, text boxes or columns
☐ Contact details in the main body, not the header
☐ Job titles that make sense to an outsider
☐ A short profile aimed at the role you want
☐ Achievements with numbers, not just duties
☐ Skills from the advert shown with evidence
☐ 2 pages, clean font, consistent dates

We've put the full screening-safe checklist inside our Career Toolkit. It needs no credits, it's just there to use.

Save this post for your next application 📌

👉 {link}

#CVTips #JobSearch #OpenToWork #CareerAdvice

items.title: What a recruiter checks in the first 30 seconds
items.body:
What does a recruiter look at in the first 30 seconds of your CV?

From our side of the desk, it's usually this:

1. Your current or last job title and company
2. How long you've stayed in your recent roles
3. Your location and whether the commute works
4. One or two achievements that prove you can do the job
5. Whether the CV is easy to read on a phone

If any of those are hard to find, the CV often doesn't get the full read it deserves.

Our free Career Toolkit checks your CV against what recruiters and screening software look for, then tells you what to fix first.

items.title: Ella: 3 fixes I make on almost every CV
items.body:
3 fixes I suggest on almost every CV I see:

1️⃣ Swap duties for results.
"Responsible for the warehouse" tells me nothing. "Ran a 40 person warehouse and cut picking errors by 30%" tells me everything.

2️⃣ Match the job title to the job you want.
If your internal title is unusual, add what it means in plain English. The screening software won't guess.

3️⃣ Move your best evidence to the top.
Your strongest achievement shouldn't be on page 2.

Want to see what your CV needs? Our free CV Health Check gives you an honest score and the fixes that matter most.

items.title: Ella: the interview question people get wrong
items.next_step: Get your free Interview Prep Pack
items.body:
"Tell me about yourself."

It's the first question in almost every interview, and it's the one people prepare for least.

What hiring managers actually want is a 60 second answer to: why are you right for this role?

Try this shape:
▪ Where you are now and what you do best
▪ One achievement that proves it
▪ Why this role is the logical next step

Our free Interview Prep Pack builds answer plans like this from your own CV and the job advert, plus the other questions you're likely to face.

items.title: Ella: quality over quantity
items.body:
"100 applications and 2 replies."

I hear versions of this from job seekers all the time, and it's rarely about ability. It's that the same CV goes to every job.

Ten applications that clearly match will beat a hundred that don't.

Before you apply, check:
✔ Do I evidence the top requirements?
✔ Is my CV aimed at this role, or at every role?
✔ Would someone see why I fit in 10 seconds?

Our free Job Match Score answers all three for any advert you paste in.

items.title: How to run the Open to Work outreach
items.body:
WHO TO FIND
▪ People with the green Open to Work frame or #OpenToWork in their headline
▪ In our sectors: engineering and technical, CAD, sales and business development, operations and logistics, purchasing and supply chain, accountancy, finance and office, IT, construction, industrial and manufacturing, driving, health and social care, catering and hospitality, corporate and HR
▪ UK based

HOW TO SEARCH
▪ People search: job title + "open to work" (for example: "maintenance engineer" "open to work"), filter Locations to the UK region
▪ Posts search: #OpenToWork + job title, sort by Latest - people posting are the most active
▪ Sales Navigator or Premium: save searches by sector so new people appear each day

DAILY RHYTHM
▪ 20 to 25 connection requests a day (LinkedIn limits weekly invites, so stay well under)
▪ Send the connection note for their sector, then the first message once they accept
▪ One polite follow-up after 5 days, then stop
▪ Log anyone promising in the Candidate Pool

RULES
▪ Always use their first name and change one line so it's personal
▪ No prices in messages. The toolkit sells the expert services on its own
▪ Use the outreach link (it tags sign-ups as li-outreach so we can see what works)
